sources.entry: Technical Overview of the 4th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable Processor Family - Where Intel states what Sapphire Rapids added: larger L2 and L3, DDR5, CXL, AMX and on-die accelerators.

summary.title: 4th Gen Intel Xeon Processor Scalable Family, Sapphire Rapids
summary.one_liner: Sapphire Rapids (4th Gen Xeon Scalable) adds DDR5, PCIe 5.0/CXL, larger caches, new memory-clustering modes, AI/crypto instructions, and built-in accelerators (QAT, IAA, DSA, AMX), compared against 3rd Gen.
keywords: cpu cache sizes l2 l3 per core
takeaways: Compares 3rd Gen and 4th Gen Xeon Scalable specs: core counts (up to 60 cores per socket), DDR5 channels, UPI speed, PCIe 5.0 and cache sizes.
Explains UMA versus sub-NUMA clustering (SNC) and the new Hemisphere and Quadrant modes, and how memory symmetry selects the mode.
Describes the new AI, crypto and virtualization instructions, including AMX, AVX-512 FP16, VPMADD52 and ENQCMD.
Covers built-in accelerators (QAT, IAA, DSA, AMX) and how they are exposed to the OS through IDXD.
summary.summary: Intel's technical overview of the 4th Gen Xeon Scalable processors (Sapphire Rapids) describes the new microarchitecture and how developers can use it. It includes a table comparing 3rd Gen and 4th Gen specs, plus a section on Optane persistent memory 200 vs 300 series. It then explains memory domain modes (UMA, sub-NUMA clustering, Hemisphere, Quadrant), the new instructions, and the built-in accelerators with their software interfaces. The page is a vendor-authored article with specification tables and architecture explanations rather than step-by-step code.
